text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod/serving latency p95 and p99 climbed above thresholds in us-west-2 (p95 ~ 850ms, p99 ~ 3.2s). Error rate (5xx/timeouts) increased 4x over baseline. Autocutover not triggered. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Priya (oncall): saw it, tails on dashboards now. Is this across all models or a single route?
Marco (infra): looks like wide fanout — gateway 502s + backend timeouts. Load looks normal, no big CPU/GPU spikes.
Alex (runtime): I'm seeing increased wait times on request multiplex queues, high connection hold durations on the dynamic router. Could be a change in the recent routing config.
Sam (sre): @deploy-bot did any deploys hit prod in the last 10m?
deploy-bot: deploy.created id=deploy-2026-03-15-21f3 sha=fb12d7 env=prod started=3122048600 finished=3122048645 by=ci/cd pipeline: rollout strategy=gradual
Priya (oncall): rollout ended ~5m ago, that aligns. Can we correlate p95 change with deploy finish?
Emma (product): customer impact: a subset of calls timed out, several large customers reported degraded responses via support. Need high-level comms if rollback required.
Alex (runtime): grabbing runtime logs. I see increased KV cache miss storm for long contexts; more mem pressure on parameter server? stack traces show stalls in response mux layer.
Marco (infra): checking infra logs: upstreams returning 524/gateway timeouts to router, not direct instance OOM. Networking team — any egress changes?
Sam (sre): running quick health checks and warmup probe for rollback candidate: 
```
# check canary
curl -sS https://prod-api.redwood.ai/health | jq '.serving.latency.p95'
```
Results: p95 from main cluster = 860ms, canary (older) = 120ms.
Priya (oncall): that gap is pretty convincing. Recommend immediate rollback of rollout (fast revert). Need signoff from infra/runtime.
Alex (runtime): agree. The new routing policy bumped multiplex queue size + adaptive batching change — that could explain larger tail latency under bursty KV misses. Rollback to previous config/sha seems safest.
Marco (infra): initiating rollback now. Command: 
```
deploy-bot rollback --id deploy-2026-03-15-21f3 --to-sha fb12d7~1 --env prod --fast
```
deploy-bot: rollback requested by Marco (infra). rollback job id=rb-3122049102 started. ETA ~90s to stop new pods and restore previous set.
incident-bot: NOTE: customer-visible errors expected to decrease as rollback completes. Continue monitoring.
Priya (oncall): watching metrics. p95 trending down: 860 -> 410 -> 180ms in 90s. p99 still elevated but dropping. 5xx rate halved.
Sam (sre): checking logs post-rollback: no new 524s from upstream, router connection hold times normalized. Running smoke harness against top customer routes.
Emma (product): support reported fewer new tickets after rollback. One large customer saw intermittent errors for ~7min window; we should draft a post-incident note.
Alex (runtime): root cause hypothesis: interaction between new routing policy and KV cache warmup causing multiplex queue blocking under certain prefix distributions. We'll reproduce in staging with similar request churn.
Marco (infra): followups: open ticket infra-3122 to add automatic rollback threshold for latency spikes during rollout; increase observability on queue lengths.
Priya (oncall): immediate mitigation done. Handing incident to Sam for postmortem & timeline. Sam, please include timeline, customer impact, and remediation owners.
Sam (sre): will do. Initial action items: reproduce in staging (Alex), add a canary test for KV miss patterns (Marco), update rollout doc to include faster abort criteria (Priya/Marco), customer comms draft (Emma).
Emma (product): I'll prepare a short customer email and support blurb with ETA for postmortem.
Priya (oncall): closing pager for now, will leave channel open for handoff notes. If any regressions/flaps appear, ping me @Priya. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: latency and error rate returned to baseline. Incident duration ~11m from alert to rollback effect.
Sam (sre): leaving notes here, tagging follow-ups. Will create postmortem PR and link runbooks.
Marco (infra): adding grafana snapshots + the rollback command output to the ticket.
Alex (runtime): will push a minimal test harness for the routing change to catch this in CI.
Emma (product): collecting affected customer list from support and prepping comms.
Priya (oncall): thanks team. Handoff complete.
